name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,721

clue.text: Tins opened by retired islanders

indicators.note: something opened has another thing let into its middle, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: tins are cans
RET is the standard abbreviation for retired

explanation.surface: Pensioners on some island prising open their tins of food.
explanation.walkthrough: RET is the usual abbreviation for retired, seen on military rank lists; it sits inside the tins after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Crete, the large Greek island in the Mediterranean, are its native inhabitants.

clue.text: Stop luggage item with E inside

indicators.note: a thing sitting inside another is enclosed by it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a case is a suitcase, an item of luggage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A customs officer halting a suitcase that has something marked E packed in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter E goes after the C of CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to an end or halt an activity, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Try being naughty over a nude

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is unruly and out of order, so the letters misbehave into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky attempt at being naughty while looking at a nude figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a positional word but it is part of the letters to rearrange, along with 'a nude'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to make an effort or attempt, so the verb works as a synonym for try.

clue.text: Cut down a middle eight

blocks.note: taken as written
in songwriting, the middle eight is the contrasting section also called the bridge

explanation.surface: A songwriter trimming the middle eight bars out of a pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle eight is the contrasting passage in a pop song, also known as the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, so the verb is a synonym for reduce in length.

clue.text: One fleecing old England striker

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who clips the wool off sheep
second meaning: a famous former England football captain and centre forward of the 1990s

explanation.surface: A former England centre forward accused of ripping people off.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleecing suggests swindling, but here it is literal sheep-clipping. Alan Shearer scored 30 goals for England's football team in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep farmer's worker removes wool, and the surname belongs to the famous retired English footballer.

clue.text: Good daughter returning salsa?

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for good
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A well-behaved daughter coming home to her salsa dancing lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Salsa looks like the dance, but the question mark flags it as a tomato sauce for crisps.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is one example of a thick sauce for dunking tortilla chips, hence the question mark for definition by example.

clue.text: Earl wears clothes for men

indicators.note: a wearer is surrounded by what is worn, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earl
duds is slang for clothes

explanation.surface: An aristocrat putting on menswear.
explanation.walkthrough: The earl sits inside the clothes, between DUD and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudes is informal American slang for guys or fellows, so it stands for men in casual speech.

clue.text: Soldier on exercises right to get serious

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
R is the abbreviation for right
a serious illness is a severe one

explanation.surface: A soldier on exercises being told to take things seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like a noun in an army scene; 'Soldier on' is the verb phrase meaning keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep going despite difficulty, which is exactly what persisting doggedly means.

clue.text: Cold run? I'll put on overcoat!

definitions.note: the definition is the answer speaking in the first person

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a run in tights or stockings is called a ladder in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone with a laddered stocking on a chilly day deciding to cover up with a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a ladder is a run in tights. The definition is a line the answer might say about itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cladder fixes cladding, an outer covering layer, to buildings, so its job is applying an external coat.

clue.text: Bread, tea and milk around India

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the opposite way, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: cha is an old slang word for tea
to milk a source is to tap it
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian meal of flatbread with milky tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around India' reads as a place but 'around' turns the milk word backwards and India is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flat bread from South Asian cooking, a specific kind of bread.

clue.text: Some top-end or second-class support?

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphenated word, the conjunction and the start of the next word
surface padding completing 'second-class'; it supplies no letters

explanation.surface: Choosing between first-class and second-class backing for a product.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from inside 'top-end' through 'or' into 'second'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or product is to back it publicly, so the verb is a synonym for back.

clue.text: A looker Hoskins picked up

indicators.note: picking up a signal means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Hoskins is the setter, and a setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The crossword setter being chatted up by an attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: A looker looks like an attractive person; here it is a literal organ that looks. The setter's name stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of sight is the part of the body that does the looking, a whimsical literal reading.

clue.text: Beer by that Bow woman drinking with king

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
X is the times sign, as in three by four
and means together with
a Cockney from Bow drops the h of her, saying 'er

explanation.surface: An East End woman sharing a pint with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockneys, who drop their aitches. The parts are loosely ordered; 'drinking' only joins the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian monarch, and several Scottish rulers also bore that name.

clue.text: Day in Kent to see Foreigner

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: WED is the abbreviation for Wednesday
Kent is a county in the South East of England

explanation.surface: Visiting Kent for a day to watch the rock band Foreigner play.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the county at England's south-east corner, so it gives SE. Foreigner looks like the rock band, capital and all.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, so to a Briton such a person is someone from abroad.

clue.text: Pal with a Garand rifle shot ...

blocks.note: taken as written
the Garand was the American M1 rifle, with the 1 read as the letter I
a shot at something is a go

explanation.surface: A friend firing an old army rifle, the story running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 Garand was the standard US infantry rifle of the Second World War; the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, borrowed into casual English for a mate or buddy.

clue.text: Shy criminal hit in bed, I admitted

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked and wrong, so the letters are set in a crooked new order
to be admitted is to be let in, so a letter is taken inside the group

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shy crook confesses to an assault in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun but is the signal to rearrange, and 'I admitted' adds one more letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhibited person is held back by self-consciousness, which is what being bashful or reserved means.

clue.text: ... a released wild animal

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disorderly, so these letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a friend shoots a wild beast that has just been freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild animal' reads as one phrase, but 'wild' is the anagram signal and 'animal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eared seals, such as sea lions and fur seals, are marine mammals with external ear flaps.

clue.text: Wally hugged by hotty on hot dryer?

indicators.note: a hugged thing is wrapped in someone's arms, so one piece is enclosed by the others

blocks.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
wally and clot are both British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A fool being hugged by an attractive person while a heated drier runs.
explanation.walkthrough: DISH placed on H makes DISHH, and the fool goes between them. Wally is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel for wiping crockery after washing up is something that dries, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Reveal song by Rod first to exec

indicators.note: the first of something is its opening letter, so only that initial is kept

blocks.note: a lay is a song or ballad
a metal rod is a bar
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Disclosing a Rod Stewart track to a record company executive first.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like Rod Stewart the singer, but it is just a metal bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something bare is an idiom for exposing or uncovering it completely, matching disclose.

clue.text: Got in the ride shaking

indicators.note: a shaken thing is jumbled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone climbing aboard a fairground ride that is rattling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got in' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Got' alone is the definition and 'in' is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To have inherited something is to have received it, usually from a relative's estate after death.

clue.text: Fills drink after win

indicators.note: one thing coming after another follows it, so the piece before this word is placed second

blocks.note: to take a prize is to win it
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Topping up glasses after a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the drink second, so the win word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes up space or time occupies it, which is how a thing fills a room or a day.

clue.text: One attending to canine in a bad way?

definitions.text: One attending to canine in a bad way?

blocks.clueFragment: One attending to canine in a bad way?
blocks.note: surface reading: a vet treating a sick dog
setter's reading: a canine is also a pointed tooth, and a bad one needs treating

explanation.walkthrough: Canine suggests a dog and a vet, but it is the pointed tooth beside the incisors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor treats decayed or damaged teeth, including the pointed teeth called canines.

clue.text: Spot duke with yen to get off

blocks.note: to spot something is to see it
D is the abbreviation for duke
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An aristocrat spotted with a craving to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like the definition (a pimple), but it is a verb giving the first piece; 'off' at the end defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling seedy or off means feeling slightly unwell, an informal British sense of both words.

clue.text: Rabbit available at eatery in the country

blocks.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering, so rabbit means gab
a dish available at a restaurant is on the menu

explanation.surface: Rabbit served at a rural restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit looks like food, but in British slang to rabbit is to chatter. 'In the country' looks like rural; only 'country' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is an independent nation on the Atlantic coast of west-central Africa.

clue.text: Young lady convict knocked up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an old lag is British slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A young woman made pregnant by a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked up' is crude slang for pregnant, but here it simply turns the word upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman, especially in American speech.

clue.text: Resort detaining English kinswoman

indicators.note: to detain is to hold someone in custody, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A female relative held by police at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a verb or a generic place; it is the Riviera city of Nice.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a daughter of one's brother or sister, so she is a female relative.

clue.text: Put out cigar and bonk Serpent

indicators.note: to be put out is to be disturbed and upset, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stubbing out a cigar and hitting a snake on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests extinguishing the cigar; it is the signal to rearrange. Bonk is British slang for a knock on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, native to the forests of South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: B___ shower head!

blocks.note: taken as written
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A blank to fill before the word shower, as if completing a phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank after the B is filled by a word for shower; the whole answer could also precede 'shower' as a punning brainstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: Head and brain are both used for the mind or intellect, as in using your head.

clue.text: Literature in post

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer: what is found in the mail

blocks.note: first meaning: learning and writing
second meaning: the written messages delivered by the postman

explanation.walkthrough: 'In post' looks like a job title (being in post) but it means items in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means literary culture in phrases like arts and letters, and the word also names mailed correspondence.

clue.text: One dead on small Ohio island

definitions.note: used as a verb: to island something is to cut it off

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another is placed after it, so the earlier piece goes last

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
O is the first letter used for Ohio, as in the state code OH
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A corpse found on a small island in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the dead word after the small Ohio pieces. Island looks like a noun but is used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To island something, in an old verbal sense, is to cut it off and set it apart like land in the sea.

clue.text: Go fast if short of time

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to fast is to go on a strict diet
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice to hurry if you are running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go fast' reads as hurry; 'Go' is the definition and 'fast' means abstain from food.
explanation.definitionFit: To go is a euphemism for passing away, as in when I go, so it means to expire.

clue.text: Long to get leg over and begin apace

indicators.note: something laid over another covers it from both sides, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
to long or itch for something is to crave it

explanation.surface: An eager rider swinging a leg over the saddle to set off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg over' is British slang for sex, a red herring; the leg word simply goes around the craving word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is an idiom for setting to work vigorously and eagerly, so it means starting energetically.
